mechanism_narrative: A sharp increase in the Federal Funds rate above 1.5% in a given month reduces near-term discount rates, lowering the present value of future equity cash flows and thereby producing negative S&P 500 20-day forward returns.
candidate_trigger: FEDFUNDS crosses above 1.5% in the current month
failure_condition: 20-day forward returns are not statistically different from zero during the identified Fed rate hike episode (p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A monthly increase in employment (PAYEMS) exceeding 20,000 jobs signals labor market strengthening, which is associated with higher consumer confidence and equity valuations, driving positive S&P 500 60-day forward returns.
failure_condition: 60-day forward returns show no statistically significant correlation with PAYEMS monthly gains (Spearman's rho < 0.2).

mechanism_narrative: A consecutive decline in industrial production (INDPRO) by at least 2% in two consecutive months indicates weakening supply-side demand, which is expected to depress corporate earnings growth and produce negative 20-day S&P 500 forward returns.
candidate_trigger: INDPRO falls by ≥2% in two consecutive months
failure_condition: 20-day forward returns are positive and statistically significant during such INDPRO declines (p < 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A sustained monthly rise in consumer price inflation (CPIAUCSL) above 0.3% for three months suggests persistent demand pressures, which can lead to higher expected future rate hikes and thereby negative 20-day S&P 500 forward returns.
failure_condition: 20-day forward returns are positive and robust across multiple inflation regimes (p < 0.05 in out-of-sample test).

mechanism_narrative: When the Unemployment Rate (UNRATE) falls below 4% for the first time in a quarter, it often precedes a dovish Fed narrative, lowering real rates and producing positive 5-day S&P 500 forward returns.
failure_condition: 5-day forward returns are negative or insignificant during such episodes (p > 0.1).

mechanism_narrative: Simultaneous increases in both retail sales (not available in catalog) and industrial production (INDPRO) are hypothesized as proxies for balanced demand growth; however, using only INDPRO, a sharp rise above 105 (current level) combined with a decline in RSAFS (durable goods orders) below 480k suggests demand softening, which predicts negative 20-day returns.
candidate_trigger: INDPRO > 105 AND RSAFS < 480,000 in the same month
regime_hint: Demand softening via durable goods weakness
failure_condition: 20-day forward returns are not negatively correlated with the combined INDPRO/RSAFS signal (Spearman's rho < -0.2).

mechanism_narrative: A sustained monthly rise in housing starts (not available) — instead, a sharp increase in HOUST (utilization rate) above 11% for two months indicates labor market overextension, which is associated with higher risk premia and negative 60-day S&P 500 forward returns.
failure_condition: 60-day forward returns are positive and statistically significant during such periods (p < 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: When the 3-month moving average of GDPC1 (GDP) exceeds 17,000 (current level), it suggests robust economic momentum that can be mispriced into equity valuations, producing positive 20-day S&P 500 forward returns unless offset by high inflation.
failure_condition: 20-day forward returns are not significantly different from zero during such episodes (p > 0.05 in walk-forward test).
